title: Shaving or trimming
hook: men shave or trim, women cut a fingertip's length

segments.voice: Yesterday: the sacrifice, its meat eaten and shared, and only the devotion reaching God. Your line: shared meat.

"And those who trim?" It's the companions asking. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has just asked God to have mercy on those who shave their heads. Some of the men listening have only trimmed theirs. So they ask: and those who trim? He repeats the prayer for those who shave. They ask again. Only after asking more than once do they hear him include them: and those who trim. A small, almost funny exchange, people making sure they're counted. Today, shaving or trimming.
screen: `MERCY ON THOSE WHO SHAVE.` → `AND THOSE WHO TRIM?` → `AND THOSE WHO TRIM.`

segments.voice: Start with why hair matters here at all. In ihram, pilgrims don't cut their hair; Surah Al-Baqarah tells them not to shave their heads until the offering has reached its place. Then, after the stoning and the sacrifice, it's cut. Anas reports in Sahih Muslim that the Prophet came back to his place at Mina, called the barber, pointed to one side of his head and then the other, and gave his hair away to the people. Second, the two ways. The hadith from the hook, in Sahih al-Bukhari, praises those who shave, and when asked, includes those who trim. Both are allowed for men. Shaving is the fuller act; trimming is enough. Third, women. A report from Ibn Abbas in Sunan Abi Dawud says women don't shave; they only shorten. Jurists describe it as cutting about a fingertip's length from the ends. Fourth, what the cut does. It marks a release. Much of what ihram held back is lifted, and the pilgrim can wear ordinary clothes again. Surah Al-Fath pictures believers entering the Sacred Mosque in safety, heads shaved and hair cut, without fear. One more thing. On that busy day people did the rites in a jumble, and came to the Prophet worried. One said he'd shaved before sacrificing. The answer, in Bukhari: do it, there's no harm. The schools of law later discussed when a change of order needs making up. But that day, the worried were met with ease. So the end of ihram is something anyone can see: a shaved head, or hair a little shorter at the ends.
screen: `DON'T SHAVE UNTIL THE OFFERING.` · `SHAVE, OR TRIM: BOTH COUNT.` · `WOMEN SHORTEN, NOT SHAVE.` · `A RELEASE FROM IHRAM.` · then, large: `DO IT, THERE'S NO HARM.`

segments.voice: Turn your hands over and look at your nails, growing all this time without any help from you, the way a pilgrim's hair grows through ihram. Let them stand for the stretch you've just come through, this week, this season, and ask whether something in it is finished. If you pray, say a quiet bismillah for what comes next; if not, just breathe.
Shaving or trimming. Men shave or trim their hair, and women cut a little from the ends, marking the release from ihram. Today's word.
Your line: a new start. Something ends, so something else can begin clean. That's day eleven thirty-five.

notes: Bukhari 1727 (also Muslim 1301): mercy for those who shave; the companions ask 'and those who trim?'. The number of repetitions differs between narrations, so no count is given. Confirm.
Muslim 1305 (Anas): the barber, right side then left, hair given to the people. Confirm number.
Abu Dawud 1984/1985 (Ibn Abbas): women do not shave, only shorten. Confirm number and grading. 'About a fingertip's length' is attributed to jurists (from the outline); confirm.
'Much of what ihram held back is lifted' (first tahallul): confirm the phrasing, including what remains restricted until the tawaf of Ifadah.

Bukhari 1736 (or 83/124): 'do it, there's no harm' about rites done out of order. The script notes the schools later discussed when a change of order needs making up (e.g. Hanafi views on dam); confirm wording.
